posts.title: Anserin's own engine under the hood
posts.details:
Before: system info, brightness, lock keys and Night light leaned on helpers from Serpantinum, and every click sound started its own player.

Now: Anserin has its own core. Sounds start in about 4 ms instead of 80 ms, wallpaper lists load small copies of your pictures (about 12x faster), video wallpapers get a real poster instead of a blank first frame, and wallpapers can sit in Images and Videos subfolders.

Nothing to set up: it builds itself the first time Anserin starts (cmake and a C++ compiler are needed; without them Anserin keeps its old ways).

posts.title: Gargantua: a black hole for your Network page
posts.details:
A new Network style. Your router sits inside a live black hole, with the Wi-Fi networks around you floating in its glow. Click one to connect.

Pick it in Edit panel → Style → Network. It has its own editor for colour, tilt and how the networks group.

posts.title: Radar: a calm map of the networks near you
posts.details:
A new Network style. The networks around you are drawn as a web of points around your router, with the one you use at the bottom and its power button beside it.

Pick it in Edit panel → Style → Network.

posts.title: Smart Weather: a sky that matches outside
posts.details:
A new Weather style, like a smart mirror. The whole page is a sky that follows the time of day and the weather now (rain, clouds, mist, snow, storms), with the hours and the next five days below.

Pick it in Edit panel → Style → Weather. Its editor lets you try any time and weather.

posts.title: Style editors use one simple bar
posts.details:
Before: a style's settings opened in a tall card beside the preview.

Now: the settings sit in one short bar above the preview, with the same buttons and sliders in every editor, so the preview stays big and in the middle.

posts.title: A heads-up before heavy styles
posts.details: Some styles use a lot more of your computer than others. Picking one of them (Gargantua, or Bubble in System) now shows a short warning with a before and after picture. Got it keeps the new style, Cancel puts the old one back.

posts.title: A new way to add widgets
posts.details:
Before: Open Redactor showed only a small bar over your desktop, and you added a widget without seeing it first.

Now: your desktop shrinks to the right with a soft bounce. Pick a group at the bottom, then a widget, and every style of it shows live on the left, two per row. Click one and it lands on your desktop. The selected widget's tools sit above it, and closing grows the desktop back.

posts.title: The old Bar popups and desktop menu are gone
posts.details:
The Volume popup, the classic Calendar and the Calendar Dashboard could only be opened from the old Bar, so they are removed. Volume, music and network live in Control Center and the left panel.

Right-clicking the desktop no longer has a hidden old menu behind it. Right-clicking a widget still opens its menu, and the desktop's actions are in the corner revolver.

posts.title: Control has one layout now
posts.details: Control Center → Control always uses the dial and cards. The older "classic" layout, and the Settings pages only it used, are removed. It could only be turned on by editing the settings file by hand.

posts.title: Update's tabs sit in the middle
posts.details:
Before: the Latest, All and Not installed buttons sat on the left, and the version and date were on a separate line under them.

Now: the buttons are in the middle, with the version on their left and the date on their right, all on one line.

posts.title: No more alerts for the version you already have
posts.details: Anserin could tell you a version was out when you already had it. Fixed.

report.where: Right after logging in or restarting Anserin
report.wrong: The update alert sometimes named the version you already had
report.changed: Anserin now waits until it knows which version you have before it compares

posts.title: See what's new in Update
posts.details:
Control Center → Update now lists every release: Latest, All, and Not installed.

When a new version is out, Anserin tells you once and can update itself with one click. It checks GitHub a minute after you log in and then every 6 hours.

Some new features will arrive turned off. Open one and press Turn on to try it, and Turn off to go back.

posts.title: The Default interface is gone
posts.details:
Anserin is now the only interface. The bar, the floating Quick Actions and the separate Settings window are removed, along with the switch between interfaces.

If you were still on the Default interface, Anserin moves you over once and keeps your settings.

posts.title: New installs start in Anserin
posts.details: A fresh install now opens the Anserin interface you see in the screenshots.

report.where: Right after installing, on the first start
report.wrong: Anserin opened the old Default interface with a bar, not the Anserin interface
report.changed: New installs start in Anserin, and the old interface is removed

posts.title: Anserin is out
posts.details:
The first public version of Anserin. It comes with the Anserin interface, the left panel with Bubble, Control Center on the right edge, the corner revolver, the duck and the Simple lock screen.

Install it with the installer, and update with anserin -up.
